newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Liberals face reduced majority - Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Canada Liberals face reduced majority - Reuters poll.

text.p: Canada's ruling Liberals are losing support, even in their Ontario stronghold, and face the prospect of a reduced majority in the June 2 election, a Reuters poll released on Tuesday showed.

The poll, the third in a series of four daily tracking polls conducted for Reuters by Zogby International, raises questions about whether Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals will retain a parliamentary majority in an election Chretien called 18 months early.
"A Liberal majority is iffy," pollster John Zogby said in a telephone interview.
A minority government "is within the realm of possibility. It's too close to call right now," he said. "Chretien will no doubt win, but his power in a second term can be greatly diminished."
In the 1993 election, the Liberals won 177 of the 295 parliamentary seats, with 41 percent of the vote.
The latest survey, conducted from May 24 to May 26, showed the Liberals with 40.7 percent of support, with their lead over the second-place Conservatives trimmed to 18.7 points.

The previous Reuters poll released on Monday showed the Liberal lead at 21.6 points, while results on Sunday showed a 23.6-point spread. A Reuters poll at the beginning of May gave the Liberals a 31.4 point lead over the Conservatives.

Tuesday's poll results showed Jean Charest's Conservatives with 22 percent of support among decided voters, the right-wing Reform Party with 18.8 percent, the left-wing New Democrats 9.3 percent and the separatist Bloc Quebecois 6.3 percent.
Undecided voters made up 28.6 percent of respondents, down slightly from Monday's 32.6 percent.

"As the Liberals' share of the vote declines, hovering around 40 percent and thus keeping the question of a majority government an open one, it becomes more clear that a united opposition front could be potent in a second term for Chretien," Zogby said.

The Reuters-Zogby poll mirrors another poll released on Tuesday suggesting a slimmer Liberal majority. The poll by Ekos Research Associates gave the Liberals 37.8 percent, with 21.2 percent for the Conservatives, 17.7 percent for Reform, 11.3 percent for the NDP and 9.7 percent for the Bloc.
"This could well be a minority with any further erosion," the Ekos pollsters said.
Canada's last minority federal government was in 1979, when Conservative leader Joe Clark defeated Pierre Trudeau's Liberals. The Clark government lasted nine months.

The Reuters-Zogby poll on Tuesday showed the Liberals still dominate vote-rich Ontario, but their support slipping to 49 percent -- under 50 percent for the first time. The Liberals won 98 of Ontario's 99 seats in 1993.
The poll showed Quebec remaining a three-way race among the Liberals, Bloc and Conservatives.
In the Maritime provinces, the Conservatives have gained on the Liberals. The Liberals have strong support in the Prairies.

Reform continues to dominate the Western provinces, with 48 percent support in Alberta and 37 percent in British Columbia. The poll showed the Liberals with 24 percent in Alberta and 31 percent in British Columbia.

The surveys are the result of a three-day rolling average of 1,115 Canadians with a margin of error of plus or minus three percent 19 times out of 20. The margin of error is wider for regional breakdowns.
